clue.text: A fish-cake

definitions.meaning: a deep-bodied sea fish caught in warm waters
a ... (Pontefract) cake is a small round liquorice sweet from Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a single fish-cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen joins two separate definitions. A Pontefract or Pomfret cake is a flat disc of liquorice made in the Yorkshire town of Pontefract.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a tropical food fish and a traditional Yorkshire liquorice sweet.

clue.text: European feline, a smelly creature

parts.note: a Pole is a native of Poland, a European
a feline is a cat

explanation.surface: A naturalist describes a European wild cat as rather smelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European feline' reads as one description, but it splits into two pieces, and the definition is the clue's second half.
explanation.definitionFit: This member of the weasel family is notorious for the foul odour it gives off when threatened.

clue.text: Losing one clergyman for church

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is taken away from the clergyman's word

parts.note: a minister is a member of the clergy
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A diocese loses one priest who served its church.
explanation.definitionFit: A great church, often one that grew from a monastery, as at York or Westminster.

clue.text: Their version of a BBC legend

indicators.note: a different version of the word their is a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: People give their own account of a broadcasting hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' tells us to rearrange the letters of 'Their'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord John Reith was the founding Director-General of the BBC and shaped its public-service ethos.

clue.text: To intimidate, to revolt, involves sin

indicators.note: involves means the first pieces wrap around the word for sin

parts.note: taken as written
to sin is to err
to revolt is to rise up

explanation.surface: A rebel's call to intimidate, to revolt, means committing a sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' places the word for sin just after the opening letter of the two-word phrase 'to revolt'; the surface's list of verbs hides that only the first is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To frighten people into submission by threats or violence.

clue.text: A Suffolk town sending bishop to greater Manchester area

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Eccles is a town in Greater Manchester, home of the Eccles cake

explanation.surface: A bishop is posted from a Suffolk town to an area of Greater Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Greater Manchester is the county around the city of Manchester; Eccles lies within it. Suffolk is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Beccles is a market town on the River Waveney in the English county of Suffolk.

clue.text: To a degree, revolutionary was exposed

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree
a Red is a revolutionary communist

explanation.surface: Someone's revolutionary past was partly brought to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a degree' looks like 'partly', but 'a degree' is BA; 'To' and 'was' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To bare something is to uncover it or lay it open to view.

clue.text: Hymns whose strange accent is Latin

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A choir sings hymns with an odd accent because they are in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' tells us to rearrange ACCENT, IS and L (Latin).
explanation.definitionFit: Canticles are sacred songs or chants taken from the Bible, such as the Magnificat, used in church services.

clue.text: Woolly jumper a woman takes to dance

parts.note: a lamb is a young sheep that is woolly and leaps about
Ada is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman puts on a woolly sweater before going dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'jumper' is the British word for a sweater, which is the surface reading; here it is an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast, sensual Brazilian partner dance that became a craze in 1989.

clue.text: Sister can see the last of a pope

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: the last points to the final letter of see

explanation.surface: A nun may finally see the pope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last' takes the final letter of 'see', not the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sistine means relating to Pope Sixtus, as in the Sistine Chapel built for Sixtus IV.

clue.text: Real kin may be taller and thinner

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could be rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Your real relatives might turn out to be taller and slimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' tells us to rearrange REAL KIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanky means tall and thin, and this is its comparative form.

clue.text: Regiment calls and calls again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army regiment
to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A regiment rings and rings again.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army. The second 'calls' is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a new title; to call it by a new label.

clue.text: Manage to hear part of phrase, a slogan

parts.note: to catch a remark is to manage to hear it
a phrase is made of words

explanation.surface: Someone strains to hear part of a phrase that is a slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchword is a popular phrase or motto repeated as a rallying cry.

clue.text: I spoil one display of Japanese porcelain

parts.note: to spoil something is to mar it
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone frets that they will ruin a display of Japanese pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Imari ware is a richly decorated porcelain exported from the port of Imari in Japan.

clue.text: Futuristic designs are on the cards

definitions.text: Futuristic designs are on the cards

parts.words: Futuristic designs are on the cards
parts.note: a deck of picture cards used by fortune-tellers to foresee the future

explanation.surface: Avant-garde patterns are about to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the cards' means likely to happen, but here the designs are literally printed on cards, and 'futuristic' because they are read to tell the future.
explanation.definitionFit: These cards with symbolic pictures are laid out by fortune-tellers to predict what lies ahead.

clue.text: Sober in the desert, or when one finds a restaurant

indicators.note: in tells us that one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means sober
to desert someone is to rat on them
taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A teetotaller in the desert wonders when they will find a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the betrayer's word inside the teetotal abbreviation. 'the desert' suggests sand dunes, but it is the verb meaning to abandon; 'the', 'when' and 'finds' are padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a simple Italian eating house serving informal meals.

clue.text: Teach to unravel clue? I can't!

indicators.note: to unravel letters is to untangle and rearrange them

explanation.surface: A frustrated student cries that they cannot work out a crossword clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unravel' tells us to rearrange CLUE, I and CANT; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To inculcate is to instil an idea in someone by persistent instruction.

clue.text: A particular peg, we're told, is a sure thing!

indicators.note: we're told signals that the words are heard spoken, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: a certain tee: certain means particular, and a tee is the golfer's peg

explanation.surface: A gambler is assured that one particular peg is guaranteed to win.
explanation.walkthrough: A tee is the small peg a golf ball sits on. 'we're told' tells us that CERTAIN TEE, said out loud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is bound to happen, like a racing favourite that cannot lose.

clue.text: Having confidential access to a pirate?

definitions.text: Having confidential access to a pirate?

parts.words: Having confidential access to a pirate?
parts.note: read as 'private ear', someone with the secret ear of a buccaneer; really a licensed sea raider

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys the confidence of a pirate.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as PRIVATE EER and it sounds like 'private ear', a confidential hearing; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was a privately owned armed ship, or its captain, licensed by a government to attack enemy shipping, close to a pirate.

clue.text: An animal with a plentiful supply of walkers

definitions.text: An animal with a plentiful supply of walkers

parts.words: An animal with a plentiful supply of walkers
parts.note: walkers are feet, and a creature with many of them, from Greek poly (many) and pod (foot)

explanation.surface: A creature is blessed with lots of hikers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walkers' looks like ramblers, but it means feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A polypod is a creature with many feet, like a millipede.

clue.text: Is it blank? The opposite

definitions.meaning: blank verse is unrhymed poetry, so a piece described as blank is written ...
the converse or reverse of something

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader asks whether a page is empty and is told the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part plays on blank verse: if a poem is blank, it is IN VERSE, read as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrhymed lines are still poetry written in metre, and the single word means directly contrary.

clue.text: A woman's place in Alabama

definitions.meaning: A city in Alabama, start of the 1965 civil-rights marches

explanation.surface: A woman's home is in Alabama.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, and the Alabama city famous for the voting-rights march to Montgomery.

clue.text: Halt! Take back all on the plate

parts.note: halt as an adjective means lame, limping

indicators.note: take back tells us to read the word all backwards

explanation.surface: A diner orders someone to stop and return everything on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halt!' looks like a command, but it is the old adjective meaning lame.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamella is a thin layer or plate, as in the gills of a mushroom.

clue.text: Two articles about grant for sportsman

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about means the articles go around the word for grant

parts.note: the is the definite article
to grant permission is to let

explanation.surface: Two newspaper pieces are about a sports grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the two articles round the word for grant, which sits between the H and the final E; 'articles' suggests newspaper pieces, but they are grammar's a and the.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a person trained in sport, especially track and field.

clue.text: Look, a tank of green colouring

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
a vat is a large tank for liquids

explanation.surface: Someone points out a vat of green dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovat is a muted greyish-green colour used in Scottish tweeds.

clue.text: Asian prince's nurse — or butler in India

parts.note: a khan is a ruler or prince in central Asia; the 's gives the letter S
an amah is a nursemaid in the East

explanation.surface: An Asian prince's nanny or his Indian butler.
explanation.definitionFit: A khansamah was the head servant or steward of a household in British India.

clue.text: A boat that goes back and forth

indicators.note: goes back and forth tells us the word reads the same in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A small craft is paddled to and fro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes back and forth' sounds like rowing, but it means the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A kayak is a light, enclosed canoe propelled by a double-bladed paddle.

clue.text: Instrument one can't stand? (Arabian)

parts.note: someone who cannot stand up would sit
Ar is an abbreviation for Arabian or Arabic

explanation.surface: An Arabian instrument that grates on the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't stand' reads as hating something; here it means not standing, so sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked Indian lute with sympathetic strings.

clue.text: Paint a seaside town with a bit of sunlight

parts.note: a port is a coastal town
a ray is a single beam of sunlight

explanation.surface: An artist paints a coastal town in a shaft of sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict someone or something in a picture.

clue.text: Girl with a brown back — an untrue statement

indicators.note: back tells us the words a brown are read in reverse

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
a lie is an untrue statement

explanation.surface: A girl's suntanned back turns out to be fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the two words 'a brown' round together, giving NATA; 'brown back' suggests a suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: Natalie is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Bike cad crashed, to expire by degrees

indicators.note: crashed signals that the letters are smashed up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A cad on a bike crashes and dies slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' tells us to rearrange BIKE CAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants die back when shoots wither progressively from the tips downwards.

clue.text: Measure years' extent

parts.note: a yard is a unit of length
an age is a long span of years

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to measure how long years last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure' looks like the verb and the definition, but it is the noun YARD; the definition is 'extent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a distance or amount reckoned in yards.
